newsitem.title: UK: No easy rule for exchange and interest rates - BOE.
newsitem.headline: No easy rule for exchange and interest rates - BOE.

text.p: There is no simple link between the exchange rate and domestic interest rates, Bank of England chief economist Mervyn King said on Thursday.

"Although the exchange rate is an important component of our assessment of the economy and the prospects for inflation, it is not wise to succumb to the superficial attraction of a 4:1, or any other n:1 rule, for linking interest rates to changes in the exchange rate," he said in the text of a speech for delivery at the National Institute of Economic and Social Research.
The 4:1 rule, a rule of thumb used by the Treasury during the 1980s, states that a four percent rise in sterling is equivalent to a one percent base rate rise.
Sterling's rally, around 17 percent on a trade-weighted basis since August, has been used by Chancellor of the Exchequer, Kenneth Clarke, to justify unchanged base rates this year.
But the Bank of England has said the rally will result in only a one-off fall in inflation in the short term.
King said any attempt to construct a simple monetary conditions index, which would add togther domestic interest rates and the exchange rate, was "akin to adding together apples and oranges".

"One refers to an exogenous instrument of monetary policy and the other an endogenous variable, which may be responding to changes in interest rates or to other shocks to either the domestic or overseas economies."
